newsitem.title: USA: baseball-HUNDLEY BREAKS CAMPY HOMER RECORD AS METS BEAT BRAVES.
newsitem.headline: baseball-HUNDLEY BREAKS CAMPY HOMER RECORD AS METS BEAT BRAVES.

text.p: Todd Hundley hammered a record-breaking homer to cap a five-run, seventh-inning rally and Lance Johnson singled home the winner in the 12th on Saturday as the Mets beat the slumping Atlanta Braves 6-5.
Hundley's three-run homer tied the score 5-5 and was his 41st of the season and broke the record for homers in a season by a catcher set by Roy Campanella of the Brooklyn Dodgers in 1953.
"I was sitting on a changeup," said Hundley, who guessed right. "When I felt it hit the bat, I knew it was gone. This record is nice, but the bottom line is winning."
Johnson won it with his 207th hit of the season -- the most in the National League since Tony Gwynn's 218 in 1987.

The sputtering Braves, who scored the first five runs of the game and had Steve Avery on the mound, had their lead in the National League East sliced to 4 1/2 games over the Montreal Expos despite a five-hit game from Terry Pendleton.

"We had a five-run lead and got beat. There's no finger-pointing, we just got beat," Braves manager Bobby Cox said after Atlanta's sixth straight loss. "I'm not going to cry about it, we've just got to go out tomorrow and play."

In Los Angeles, Mike Piazza homered and drove in three runs and Greg Gagne and pinch-hitter Billy Ashley added three-run shots as the Los Angeles Dodgers remained atop the National League West by beating the St. Louis Cardinals 9-5.
Piazza had a run-scoring single in the first, but St. Louis rallied for a 2-1 lead before Gagne connected off starter Andy Benes (17-10) with two out in the sixth to put the Dodgers ahead to stay.
Piazza added a two-run blast in the seventh to extend the lead to 6-2 and Ashley closed the scoring one inning later with his fourth pinch hit homer of the season.
Ramon Martinez (13-6) won his fifth straight decision.

In San Diego, Jody Reed's single with two out in the bottom of the 12th inning scored Greg Vaughn from second with the winning run and lifted the San Diego Padres to a 3-2 victory over the Cincinnati Reds.

Lee Smith (3-4) retired the first two batters in the 12th before Vaughn walked and stole second. After Wally Joyner was intentionally walked, Reed slapped a 2-2 pitch to right field for the game-winner.
"Things like this happen for teams in order for them to win divisions, and things are happening for us," Reed said.
Reliever Dario Veras (2-0) pitched one inning to pick up the win for San Diego, who trail the Dodgers by half a game in the National League West.
At Colorado, Ellis Burks went 3-for-3, drove in a pair of runs and set a franchise record for hits in a season as the Colorado Rockies won their seventh straight game, 7-3 over the Houston Astros.

Burks' two-run single in a five-run third inning tied Dante Bichette's club record of 197 hits, set last season. Burks added a single in the fifth to break the record and another hit in the seventh for Colorado, which remained five games behind San Diego in the National League wild card race.
The Astros are 2 1/2 games behind the first-place St. Louis Cardinals in the NL Central Division.
Kevin Ritz (16-10) notched the victory for Colorado, who are a league-best 52-22 at home. Astro starter Donne Wall (9-7) lost his third consecutive game.

In Montreal, Mike Lansing's eighth-inning double scored Mark Grudzielanek with the go-ahead run and four relievers allowed two hits over the final four innings as the Montreal Expos edged the Florida Marlins 3-2.
Montreal, winners of 11 of their last 15 games, remain one-half game behind San Diego for the wild-card berth and just 4 1/2 games behind first-place Atlanta in the NL East.

The Expos scored a pair in the seventh to tie the game 2-2 before going in the eighth to make a winner out of reliever Dave Veres (6-3), who allowed one hit and fanned two in the eighth for his second win in three days.
In Chicago, Kevin Stocker collected a career-high four hits and Benito Santiago belted a two-run homer in the fourth inning to give the Philadelphia Phillies a 6-2 win over the Chicago Cubs.
Mike Mimbs (3-8) earned the victory. Chicago dropped 7 1/2 games out of the wild card playoff spot with 15 games left.
In San Francisco, Mike Kingery's two-out double in the top of the 12th scored Mark Johnson and Tony Womack with the go-ahead runs as the Pittsburgh Pirates defeated the San Francisco Giants 7-5.
John Ericks (4-5) pitched two scoreless innings for the win.
